page: Amazon Web Services m6in.16xlarge is a general-purpose, network-optimized virtual server instance based on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by a 3.5 GHz third-generation Intel Xeon Scalable 8375C processor with x86_64 architecture, providing 64 vCPUs across 32 dedicated physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Memory capacity is 256 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4 GB per virtual core. The instance includes hardware instruction support for AVX-512 with VNNI, VAES, and Total Memory Encryption, but contains zero GPUs and provides no bundled local NVMe storage, requiring network-attached storage via Amazon EBS.

A central feature of the m6in.16xlarge is its high-throughput network subsystem, providing a 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. In benchmark testing, the platform shows top-quartile performance in tasks leveraging hardware-accelerated instruction sets and high networking limits, including PassMark CPU encryption, database operations, static web serving throughput (44.25 GB/sec), and Clang software compilation. Multi-core compute performance on stress-ng and raw memory bandwidth fall into median performance bands, indicating steady, predictable throughput across general computational profiles rather than extreme per-core burst compute.

From a cost efficiency standpoint, the m6in.16xlarge is resource-dense and optimized for architectures where standard general-purpose computing meets high network transit requirements. Because there is no bundled local storage, users avoid paying for unused local NVMe volumes, though sustained I/O performance relies on Amazon EBS provisioning. The server is well matched for high-traffic web serving fleets, distributed database clusters, continuous integration compilation engines, and network-intensive backend services.
description: Amazon Web Services m6in.16xlarge is a general-purpose, network-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by an Intel Xeon 8375C processor. It provides 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores at 3.5 GHz, paired with 256 GB of DDR4 memory and a 100 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance lacks local storage and hardware GPU acceleration, relying on network-attached EBS volumes for persistent disk storage. Benchmark results show strong performance in static web serving throughput, PassMark database operations, cryptographic workloads, and software compilation via Clang, alongside average results in general multi-core stress testing and memory bandwidth. The balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio and 100 Gbps networking make it an efficient hardware profile for high-concurrency network tasks, distributed database layers, CI/CD build environments, and containerized enterprise services.
